newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Moeller posts 22 percent rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Moeller posts 22 percent rise in profits.

text.p: Danish shipping, oil and gas heavyweight A.P. Moeller on Thursday reported a 22 percent rise in 1996 group profits and said it saw favourable prospects for shipping and oil production in 1997.

The company, Denmark's biggest with market capitalisation of around $10.5 billion, announced a rise in group net profits to 2.2 billion crowns ($335.3 million) in 1996 from 1.8 billion the previous year on turnover of 33.0 billion crowns from 28.5 billion.
The bulk of the money came from shipping operations, which earned a net two billion crowns, up from 1.59 billion in 1995. The group expects them to do better still in 1997.
"Container liner services improved, with a result well above that of 1995. The entire Maersk Line organisation succeeded in reducing unit costs," the report said.

But it added that earnings for very large crude carriers remained unsatisfactory, despite increased activity and slightly higher rates, and that gas carriers were also disappointing. Product carriers produced acceptable profits, it said.
"In 1997 a continued increase in cargo volumes and in the result for the container liner services is expected," the report said in its outlook for the coming year.
Chief Executive Jess Soederberg said he was satisfied with the result, saying: "We are happy with the result that we achieved in 1996, I won't make any secret of it."
The most dramatic rise came from international oil operations, which turned in a profit of 279 million crowns after a loss of 103 million in 1995.

"The Maersk Olie og Gas A/S Group had, in 1996, its first year with profits from international oil activity. Oil production in Qatar increased from one million tonnes in 1995 to 1.7 million tonnes in 1996 and the oil price was somewhat above that of 1995," it said.
It added that it was continuing to invest heavily in exploration and field development, primarily in Qatar and Algeria.

Home-produced oil also played a role. Moeller's partnership with Royal Dutch/Shell and Texaco in the Danish underground consortium earned it a net 216 million crowns from North Sea production, up from 1995's bumper 212 million.
"In 1996 Dansk Undergrund's Consortium's production of oil from the North Sea set a record, with 10.4 million tonnes, approximately 12 percent above that of 1995," the report said.

"Gas sales amounted to 5.7 billion cubic metres, approximately 12 percent above those of the previous year. The average oil price was approximately $20.70 per barrel compared to approximately $17 in 1995," it added. ($ = 6.561 Danish Crowns)
